construct: RULED, THE K2 CELL (refreshed 2026-09-21): k2_overview 40–70w (the persona's current in the element's arena) + k2_functional ≤22w (the god's own family function, re-ruled 2026-09-01) + k2_domain_readings 18–55w per ruled domain (owner construct 2026-08-19, corpus ×50 LOCKED) · adj_chips {catalyst ×3, friction ×3} 1–3w under THE KEYWORD DERIVATION CHAIN (2026-09-03) and THE VOCABULARY ZONE B1–B2 (2026-09-04) · fn_reading = the weighted three-door ledger {word, doors:{trait, scene, outside}} ×3 per pole, 35–55w per door (THE THREE DOORS 2026-09-03; corpus ×50 complete 2026-09-04) · structural_interaction = the REA_03 §4b authoring seed · k2_card = the unauthored register stub (REA_03 §4, superseded by the cell above). Prompts: REA_17 §3.4. · edge (catalyst pole only; owner 2026-10-16, THE EDGE v9: two sentences, the energy and its three ruling domains from the GOD table, then a clause per domain in The Pattern's voice; the metric; the head derived in the app)

candidates.structural_interaction: Fire generating Earth cross-polarity — warmth building structure beyond expectation
candidates.k2_overview: Your Earth moves as the Virtuoso: ground that refuses to stay flat. You produce solid, startling things, the building nobody zoned, the old order reimagined from bedrock. Your rebellion wears work boots. It shows up early, builds the alternative, and lets the results argue. Slow genius, permanent output.
candidates.k2_functional: You express in built things: the model, the prototype, the standing proof.

k2_domain_readings.Talent: Your talent is constructive genius: making real what others only pitch. It compounds with patience, so pick projects worth years. Your monuments will outlast every clever thing said about them.
k2_domain_readings.Performance: You perform through results: the opening day, the finished span, the harvest weighed. Let there be openings, invite people to what you built. Even mountains benefit from an unveiling.
k2_domain_readings.Defiance: Your defiance is seismic: rare, slow, landscape-changing. When you finally move against a structure, you replace it. Use that power on things that matter, not on every irritating fence.

angles.drive: Proving a point matters more to you than making it. Because a finished thing argues better than you could out loud, you would rather prove an idea than pitch it. You pay in time, and you get to be right in a way that lasts.
angles.cost_self: Proving it is the only kind of winning you trust. Since you prove rather than pitch, you let the chances that needed a quick yes go by. You lose credit for ideas that were yours first, so pitch one before the proof is done.
angles.cost_others: You prove an idea before you share it. Whenever you would rather show a result than explain a plan, you keep people out of it until it is done. Tell one person the plan early, since a surprise is harder to help than a sketch.

angles.drive: Speaking plainly comes easier to you than softening it. Since a true thing said flat feels more honest than a kind thing dressed up, you speak plainly rather than nicely. You pay for it in warmth, and to you the truth is worth it.
angles.cost_self: Speaking plainly is how you stay honest with yourself. You would rather be understood than liked, so you say what goes unsaid and give up the easy welcome of keeping quiet. Soften one true thing a week, because you wanted that welcome too.
angles.cost_others: You speak plainly to the people who matter most to you. Where the truth counts for more than the landing, you hand it over without the cushion it needed. Add the cushion sometimes, because you want them to land softly too.

angles.drive: Rules read to you as first drafts. Since you would rather fix a bad rule than follow it, you rewrite it in the doing and in plain sight. You spend a while being marked wrong, and the rewrite tends to look like sense later.
angles.cost_self: Rewriting a rule is your answer to one that makes no sense. Each time you choose to fix it rather than obey it, you lose the credit that following it would earn. Follow one you dislike this month, because that approval was yours too.
angles.cost_others: You rewrite a rule that stops making sense under the people standing on it. Since you fix it ahead of keeping the peace, you change the footing with no warning. Give the warning first, because the rule you found pointless was somebody's floor.

angles.drive: Pushing back is your first reply to almost anything. Because agreeing feels like giving something up, you push against a plan rather than check if you mind it. Keep in mind, pushing back costs you the same whether the plan was good or not.
angles.cost_self: Pushing back is how you keep hold of yourself in a group. Since giving in feels like disappearing, you push against help as much as against orders. Remember that what you keep pushing away is help you needed.
angles.cost_others: You push back before you hear the end of a plan. Where being hard to convince feels like being hard to fool, you make people defend a plan instead of taking it. You cost them the ease of offering, and you know it.

angles.drive: Saying too much is the honesty you were built for. A thought left unsaid feels like a lie to you, so you say the whole thing rather than the useful half. Remember that the useful half was the only part you were asked for.
angles.cost_self: Saying too much proves to you that you were listening. Since a held tongue feels like a wasted turn, you spend your standing on the extra line instead of the needed one. You know the trust you talk away comes back slower than it left.
angles.cost_others: You say too much to whoever let you speak. Because a thought feels wasted unless it is said, you take their turn as much as your own. You owe whoever you talked over the sentence you took.

angles.drive: Overdoing it is the only way you know to be sure of enough. Since plain and finished feels like settling, you make it bigger rather than call it done. You pay for the extra out of yourself, a price worth keeping in mind.
angles.cost_self: Overdoing it is how you make sure a thing looks like you. Long after the plain version would do, you keep adding rather than finishing and spend what the end needed. You pay for every extra in the sleep the finish was owed.
angles.cost_others: You overdo it for people who asked for something modest. Since a plain job feels beneath what you can do, you hand them a bigger thing later instead of the small thing now. You owed them the small one now, the one with a use.

edge.lead: Earth runs through your mind, your career and your social life. It is the question you ask once everyone else has agreed, the odd way of working that is left alone because it works, and the dry joke that says the true thing out loud.
